newsitem.title: USA: Kentucky Electric sees earnings hurt by shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Kentucky Electric sees earnings hurt by shutdown.

text.p: Kentucky Electric Steel Inc said earnings for the quarter will be adversely impacted following a shutdown of its melt shop operations on Tuesday, when monitors detected a radioactive substance in baghouse dust, a by-product of the melting process.
The company's current quarter ends June 30.

Other operations have not been affected at this time. The company said it believes that the source of the radiation may have been buried in a shipment of scrap metal and was undetected by monitors that check incoming scrap.

The company said that its environmental and safety personnel are working with outside consultants and the appropriate governmental agencies to develop a clean-up and disposal plan for the dust contaminated with cesium, and expects to have a final plan in two or three days.

Kentucky Electric maintains both radiation contamination and business interruption insurance. It said that while the incident will negatively impact earnings for the quarter, it hopes that the impact on financial results will be minimal.
The company is assessing the financial impact of the damage as well as the recoverability of clean-up and disposal costs through insurance.
Kentucky Electric Steel makes special quality steel bar flats for the leaf-spring suspension, cold drawn bar conversion, truck trailer support beam and steel service center markets.
